subject: Computer Science
board: Pearson Edexcel Level 1/Level 2 GCSE (9-1) in Computer Science (1CP2)

lessons.title: Relational operators: comparing values in Python
lessons.bigQuestion: How does a program decide whether something is true or false?
objectives: Predict whether a comparison is True or False
Use comparisons in if statements and loops
successCriteria: Most: use all six relational operators in conditions
Some: debug conditions that confuse = with == or use the wrong boundary

keywords.def: compares two values and gives True or False
a value that is either True or False
an expression a program tests to make a decision
storing a value in a variable using =
the value at which a comparison changes result

starter: Bismillah. What is the result of 7 % 3 and 7 // 3?
Name the data type of 3.5 and of 'hello'.
What does the AND operator return if one input is False?

teach.heading: Comparing values
bullets: A relational operator compares and returns True or False.
teach.note: Show the six in a table with a Python example. Make the point that the result is a Boolean, not a number. Let pupils predict: 5 > 3, 5 == 3, 5 != 3. Edexcel examines Python so use exactly these symbols.

teach.heading: = versus ==
teach.note: This is the most common syntax error. One equals sign stores a value; two equals signs ask a question. Show the output of the code. Ask pupils what happens in an if statement if they write if age = 18.

teach.heading: Conditions in selection
teach.note: Trace the code with age 16, then with 18. The boundary is the key: age >= 18 includes 18, age > 18 does not. Ask which operator is needed for 'at least 18'. Link to testing boundary data from the testing lesson.

teach.heading: Worked example
teach.note: Walk through the three tests: the first condition False, so skip; second True. Emphasise that only the first True branch runs.

model.problem: A cinema discount is for score >= 50. What is printed for score = 50 and score = 49?
steps: score = 49: 49 >= 50 is False, so no discount
Changing >= to > would remove the discount for 50

teach.heading: Hinge question
teach.note: Answer C. A sets the value. B tests greater than. D is not equal. Use whiteboards.

check.q: Which line tests whether the variable password is equal to the string "salam"?
check.why: == tests equality. A single = would assign the value.

practice: Write a condition to test that a number n is at least 10 and not equal to 15.
independent: Core: Write a program that asks for a mark and prints 'Pass' if the mark is 40 or more, otherwise 'Fail'.
Extend: Write a program that asks for a password and prints 'Access granted' only if it is equal to a stored value; otherwise 'Try again'.
Stretch: A program says if score > 50 but the rules say 50 passes. Find and fix the error, then list two test values that show the problem. (3 marks)
exit: Write the Python symbol for 'less than or equal to'.
lessons.homework: Write five comparisons that evaluate to True and five that evaluate to False, using all six relational operators.
lessons.send: SEND: operator cards with examples; sentence stems. EAL: 'equal' versus 'not equal' vocabulary. Stretch: chain a comparison like 18 <= age < 65.
